label: rem:ns-kummer-specialisation-consequence
title: Consequence for NS regularity
html:
A valid QOU constrained by \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 is NS-singular: \mathrm{Obs}_\partial(A) = 0. The boundary observability vanishes. The classical Navier--Stokes equation permits finite-time blowup.

This result stems from the complementary-subgroup argument (item 3). The core topological obstruction e(\xi)|_\Sigma \neq 0 lacks any mathematical channel to suffer cancellation against the operative analytic correction \delta_n|_\Sigma. They strictly populate complementary summands inside H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).

Scope. This consequence is not established: item 3 of QU-to-QOU holds in the Kummer tower rather than as a complementary-subgroup splitting in the jet tower. On a closed surface H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) = 0, so there are no complementary summands in it, and the restriction e(\xi)|_\Sigma to the one-dimensional collision locus vanishes identically because H^2(\Sigma, \cdot) = 0. What holds unconditionally is the Kummer specialisation itself: the global class \chi(A) \bmod n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) is non-zero for n \nmid 6. That is a statement about n-th roots of the Reeb bundle, not a regularity verdict, so the classical blowup claim above is not established here.
